## SECTION 3: BRING-DOWN REPRESENTATIONS & COVENANTS

### 3.1 Bring-Down Standard

Per **SPA §7.2(a)** (Buyer's closing condition — accuracy of Seller's representations):

- **General Reps:** Must be true and correct in all material respects as of the Closing Date as though made on and as of the Closing Date (other than representations made as of a specific date, which must be true and correct as of that date).
- **Fundamental Reps** (Organization, Authorization, Capitalization, Brokers, Title to Shares): Must be true and correct in all respects (no materiality qualifier / no Material Adverse Effect qualifier).
- **MAE-Qualified Reps:** Must be true and correct except where the failure to be true and correct would not, individually or in the aggregate, constitute a Material Adverse Effect.

Per **SPA §8.2(a)** (Seller's closing condition — accuracy of Buyer's representations):

- **General Reps:** Must be true and correct in all material respects as of the Closing Date.
- **Fundamental Reps** (Organization, Authorization, Sufficiency of Funds/Financing): Must be true and correct in all respects.

## SECTION 5: CLOSING CALL AGENDA & LOGISTICS

### 5.1 Pre-Closing Call (T-1 Business Day)

**Participants:** Buyer Counsel, Seller Counsel, Financial Advisors, Escrow Agent, Deal Teams
**Agenda:**

1. Confirm all closing conditions satisfied or waived (§7.2, §8.2 checklists)
2. Walk through Funds Flow Memorandum line by line — confirm wire amounts, ABA routing, account numbers
3. Confirm escrow agent has received fully executed Escrow Agreement
4. Confirm bring-down certificates are in agreed form and ready for execution
5. Confirm all third-party consents received (or confirm which are subject to fallback treatment)
6. Review open issues from Section 4 — confirm resolution status
7. Confirm document circulation plan: who sends what, to whom, and in what sequence
8. Confirm wire funding timeline and sequential release mechanics

### 5.2 Closing Sequence (Day of Closing)

> Closing is structured as a **simultaneous exchange** — no party's documents or funds are released until all conditions are confirmed met.

```
STEP 1 (8:00 a.m. ET):  Buyer funds escrow with full wire per Funds Flow
STEP 2 (8:30 a.m. ET):  Escrow Agent confirms receipt of funds; notifies Deal Counsel
STEP 3 (9:00 a.m. ET):  All closing documents circulated via DocuSign / encrypted email
STEP 4 (9:30 a.m. ET):  All parties execute bring-down certificates and officer's certificates
STEP 5 (10:00 a.m. ET): Seller Counsel confirms receipt of all Buyer documents; 
                          Buyer Counsel confirms receipt of all Seller documents
STEP 6 (10:15 a.m. ET): Mutual written confirmation from all counsel: "Closing Declared"
STEP 7 (10:30 a.m. ET): Escrow Agent releases funds per Funds Flow:
                          (a) Payoff letters funded to Lenders
                          (b) Transaction expenses funded to Seller advisors
                          (c) Net Purchase Price released to Sellers' designated accounts
                          (d) Indemnity escrow portion retained by Escrow Agent
STEP 8 (Post-Closing):   UCC-3 terminations filed; equity transfer recorded; 
                          post-closing notifications sent
```

## SECTION 6: MATERIAL ADVERSE EFFECT — BRING-DOWN ASSESSMENT

### 6.1 MAE Definition Reference (Per SPA)

"**Material Adverse Effect**" means any change, event, occurrence, state of facts, or development that, individually or in the aggregate, has had or would reasonably be expected to have a material adverse effect on (a) the business, financial condition, assets, or results of operations of the Company and its Subsidiaries, taken as a whole, or (b) the ability of the Sellers to consummate the transactions contemplated hereby; **provided, however**, that none of the following shall constitute, or be taken into account in determining whether there has been, a Material Adverse Effect:

*(i) general economic, financial market, or political conditions;*
*(ii) conditions generally affecting the industry in which the Company operates;*
*(iii) changes in Law or GAAP;*
*(iv) acts of war, terrorism, natural disasters, or pandemics;*
*(v) the announcement or pendency of the transactions contemplated hereby;*
*(vi) any failure by the Company to meet projections or forecasts (but not the underlying facts giving rise to such failure);*
*(vii) any action taken or omitted by Sellers at Buyer's written request;*

**except**, in each case of (i)–(iv), to the extent such matters have a disproportionate adverse effect on the Company relative to other participants in the Company's industry.
